subject: Cross-region egress degradation: cutover confirmation & KV-cache validation
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: ops@stormlytics.com, alice@stormlytics.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: Cross-region egress degradation — temporary cutover instructions

Hi Alice / Stormlytics ops team,

We’re seeing a provider-level egress degradation that started at ~08:40 UTC affecting traffic to our EU and APAC edge POPs. Your tenant (stormlytics-prod / tenant-id: st-9241) shows elevated token latency (95th p50->p95) and ~12% request failures for EU endpoints.

Immediate guidance (what to do now):
- Switch your integration to the region-agnostic fallback endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/fallback (this routes to non-affected WAN paths).
- Add the header: X-Redwood-Fallback: prefer to enforce the fallback for 30m.
- Run basic KV-cache validation after cutover (steps attached): send the 3 warmup calls in cutover-checklist.pdf and confirm cache_hit_rate > 70% in the returned diagnostics.

We’ve opened an incident with the provider and are executing an automated cutover for customers who opt in. If you want us to perform the cutover for your tenant, reply with: "Please cut over stormlytics-prod now." If you prefer to handle it, switch your endpoint and run the validation steps in the checklist.

Expected impact during cutover: short bursts of increased latency (1–3s) for the first 2–3 requests while the cache warms; majority of requests should normalize within 10 minutes.

Attachments: 20270714-cutover-checklist.pdf (step-by-step), kv-cache-validation-log-20270714.txt (empty template for logs).

Sorry for the disruption — we’ll provide a follow-up with confirmed mitigation and a post-incident summary.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0189

Vivek — quick update from Ops: provider telemetry indicates a partial BGP flap on the provider’s EU peering cluster, and a downstream egress ACL misconfiguration in APAC for certain ISPs. We have two parallel mitigations in motion:

1) Automated customer opt-in cutover to fallback endpoints (will route via alternate egress for affected regions). I’ve queued stormlytics-prod for cutover; we’ll wait for their reply unless they explicitly prefer manual.
2) A targeted prefix rewrite for APAC via our transit partner (takes ~20–30m to propagate).

Jordan: start the cutover for any customers that replied "Please cut over" and push the temporary routing flag (runbook link below). Ben: please validate the KV cache warmup probe sequence and put the first run’s logs into the shared drive.

Runbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/cutover-runbook-2027 (Section 4: Temporary endpoint rollout)

Neha

Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: ops@stormlytics.com, alice@stormlytics.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, cloud-contacts@infra-partners.io
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary: provider egress disruption (EU/APAC) — cutover validation and follow-ups

Hi Sam / Alice / Stormlytics team,

Thank you for confirming opt-in on Jul 14. This is a short post-incident summary and the verification evidence from our side.

What happened (brief):
- 2027-07-14 08:40 UTC: provider reported and we observed degraded egress from several EU and APAC POPs. Root cause: a combination of (a) transient BGP instability in the provider’s EU peering plane and (b) an accidental ACL deployment that blocked specific transit prefixes in one APAC ISP zone.

What we did:
- Executed opt-in cutover for stormlytics-prod at 09:18 PDT (16:18 UTC) and routed traffic to our alternate egress path.
- Ran KV-cache warmup probe sequence (3 calls) as per the attached checklist. First-run cache_hit_rate: 76% (attached log: kv-cache-validation-log-20270714.txt).
- Confirmed 95th percentile latency returned to normal within ~9 minutes for the fallback route.

Customer observable impact:
- Short elevated latencies for the first 2–4 requests post-cutover (1–3s).
- No sustained request failures after the fallback was applied.

Attachments and evidence: 20270714-cutover-checklist.pdf, kv-cache-validation-log-20270714.txt, postmortem-draft-20270716.md

Follow-up actions we’re taking (owned by):
- (INF-4821) Provider: demand permanent peering remediation and post-change verification (Owner: Network Partnerships).
- (INF-4822) Ops: add an extra KV-cache warmup probe to the automated cutover flow to reach 85% cache_hit target (Owner: Neha Kapoor).
- (INF-4823) Product: create in-console "Fallback opt-in" toggle and alert customers on the impacted routes (Owner: Jordan Blake).

SLA / credit: We are evaluating the incident window for potential SLA credit; we’ll follow up with formal billing adjustment steps by 2027-07-20.

If you’d like a walkthrough of the logs or a short postmortem call, we can schedule 30 minutes next week. Thanks again for the quick confirmation which helped avoid larger customer impact.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
